learning_objective: 🎯 You will discover how to point out and specify nouns exactly using little but powerful words called determiners and articles!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A determiner is a word placed right before a noun to make it clear what the noun refers to. Words like 'this', 'that', 'some', 'many', and 'my' are determiners that fix the meaning of the noun!

We use 'A' and 'An' when we talk about a general person or thing, not a specific one. Use 'A' before consonant sounds (a book) and 'An' before vowel sounds (an apple). Notice we said sounds, not just letters!
The word 'The' is the definite article. We use it when we are talking about a very specific noun that the listener already knows about, or for unique things like 'The Sun' and 'The Earth'.

fun_activity.title: ✍️ The Kitchen Article Hunt
fun_activity.instructions: Go to your kitchen and pick 5 items. Write a sentence for each using the correct article (A, An, or The) before the item's name!

quick_recap: ⭐ Determiners are words placed before nouns to specify them.
⭐ Articles (A, An, The) are the most common determiners.
⭐ 'A' and 'An' are indefinite and used for general things based on starting sounds.
⭐ 'The' is definite and used for specific or unique things.
